audit.why: 51.87% over 2433 games with LeBlanc holding all seven stages. Xerath has zero mobility and one point of CC, so a chart that never flips is defensible; no rows moved and both layers already agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Late-game spike text treated Rite of the Arcane as a 'global execute' and referenced a nonexistent 'Locus of Power' range extension.
audit.why: Rite of the Arcane is 5000 range, not global, costs 100 mana on 130/115/100s, and immobilises Xerath while he fires. Locus of Power was removed from his kit and is not in Riot's data.
audit.corrected: Spikes and wants.foe now use the real range, cooldown and the self-root drawback.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated: Rite of the Arcane is a channel and your Ethereal Chains cancels it.
audit.why: Riot's R carries the channel flag ('interruptible — any CC cancels it'). Ethereal Chains (E, 925 range, 14s at rank 1) shackles on contact, and Mimic gives you a second one — either cancels a 130-second ultimate outright. Nothing on the page mentioned it.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.carry, whys[4], spikes[1], spikes[3], mid and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fabricated ability names and a wrong CC type: 'Arcane Barrage', 'Mage Chains', 'Locus of Power', and Shocking Orb described as a 'knockup-root'.
audit.why: Riot's names are Arcanopulse (Q, 750 range, 9/8/7/6/5s), Eye of Destruction (W, 1000 range), Shocking Orb (E, 1050 range, 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s) — and Shocking Orb is a stun, not a knockup or a root.
audit.corrected: All four replaced with the real names and effect.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Check it before every step-up. - W Distortion (return) is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Shocking Orb (E): 13s at rank 1, 11s at rank 5 — his only CC; dodge it and the artillery never converts. That is your entry window. - Arcanopulse (Q) is 9s at rank 1. - Rite of the Arcane is a 130s channel your Ethereal Chains cancels.

edits.before: Q the sigil, W the detonation, return before the answer — a half-bar round trip he experienced as weather.
edits.after: At 6, Mimic a second Ethereal Chains: chain, sigil, mimic-chain, and he is held through every escape he owns.

edits.before: Xerath burns Shocking Orb (Stun) on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Xerath burns Shocking Orb on a minion — that is a 13-second invitation to take plates.

edits.before: Staying at the W landing spot for one more auto — the return timer is your champion; outliving it is optional.
edits.after: Coast and he reaches Rite of the Arcane, 5000 range of free damage — end it while he is stuck at 750.

edits.before: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb (Stun), denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Xerath wins by stunning you at 1050 range, chipping with Arcanopulse from 750, and never letting you inside.

edits.before: Carry through picks — one chained carry per objective; your job is the flank angle and the discipline to leave after.
edits.after: Carry through picks — chain his 130s Rite of the Arcane mid-channel; without it he is a 750-range mage with no exit.

edits.before: If Xerath opens the score, reset expectations and respect Shocking Orb (Stun) doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with W clears and stay relevant through chain picks.
edits.after: If Xerath opens the score, stop walking into his 1050-range Shocking Orb and farm from behind the wave. After a second kill: W-clear, hold your chain for his ultimate channel, and take picks off-lane.

edits.before: His only defensive tool is a short root on cooldown, so most direct trades favor your burst once you're in range
edits.after: His only defensive tool is Shocking Orb on a 13-second cooldown, so direct trades favor your burst once you're in range

edits.before: Your burst still one-shots him at level 6 in a direct fight, since his Rite of the Arcane doesn't help him survive point-blank
edits.after: Your burst still one-shots him at level 6, and Ethereal Chains cancels Rite of the Arcane outright the moment he starts the channel

edits.before: Your burst threatens lethal before his Rite of the Arcane global ultimate matters in lane, and Distortion lets you dodge Arcane Barrage poke while closing distance.
edits.after: Your burst threatens lethal before Rite of the Arcane matters in lane, and your chain cancels that channel outright — Distortion closes the gap straight through Arcanopulse poke.

edits.before: Xerath's siege-range poke and Rite of the Arcane global executes become dangerous from max range in teamfights, but up close he still dies instantly to your burst.
edits.after: Xerath's 5000-range Rite of the Arcane punishes teamfights, but the channel holds him still — chain it and he dies, and up close he dies to your burst anyway.

edits.before: Xerath's poke is real but his complete lack of mobility means once you close the gap with E-Q, he has no way to disengage, so bait his root with your W clone then dash in. Most exchanges before level 3 favor you as long as you play around his knockup-root cooldown and don't walk into Arcane Barrage blind.
edits.after: Xerath's poke is real but his complete lack of mobility means once you close the gap with E-Q, he has no way to disengage, so bait his stun with your W clone then dash in. Most exchanges before level 3 favor you as long as you play around Shocking Orb's 13-second cooldown and don't walk into Arcanopulse blind.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 stay heavily in your favor since Distortion lets you close his siege range faster than he can kite, and once you're on top of him your burst kills him outright — his kit simply has no answer to a mobile assassin in his face. His Rite of the Arcane global ult matters more for map pressure than winning your lane directly.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 stay heavily in your favor since Distortion lets you close his siege range faster than he can kite, and once you're on top of him your burst kills him outright — his kit has no answer to a mobile assassin in his face. Rite of the Arcane is a 130-second channel: hold Ethereal Chains for it and he loses the ultimate and the fight.

edits.before: Xerath's teamfight poke and global execute threat from Rite of the Arcane make him dangerous at range late, but that threat evaporates the moment you close distance — your burst still one-shots him if you flank through stealth or dash in past his knockup-root. Respect his poke when approaching, but the actual duel remains yours.
edits.after: Xerath's teamfight poke and Rite of the Arcane from 5000 range make him dangerous late, but that threat evaporates the moment you close distance — and the ultimate is a channel your Ethereal Chains cancels outright. Respect Arcanopulse on the approach, but the duel, and the counter-engage, both remain yours.

edits.before: Poke from max range with Arcane Barrage and Mage Chains
edits.after: Poke from max range with Arcanopulse and Eye of Destruction

edits.before: Root you to prevent your engage
edits.after: Stun you with Shocking Orb to stop the engage

edits.before: Snipe kills globally with Rite of the Arcane
edits.after: Snipe from 5000 range with Rite of the Arcane

edits.before: Kite backward using Locus of Power range extension
edits.after: Kite backward and channel Rite of the Arcane safely

notes: Chart untouched — packet and both page layers already agree on LeBlanc 7/7, which matches the 51.87% win rate and Xerath's zero-mobility kit. Three fabricated ability names were on this page ('Arcane Barrage', 'Mage Chains', 'Locus of Power') plus Shocking Orb described as a knockup-root; all corrected from Riot's data. All three lintFindings fixed. Riot's R text is terse ('immobilizes himself and gains numerous long-range barrages') and does not state the barrage count or whether the self-immobilise can be cancelled by Xerath himself, so no claim was made about either.
